title: Functions & calls
theory:
## Procedures

Use `call label` to push the return address and jump; `ret` pops it back. Keep the stack **16-byte aligned** before `call` when you will reach libc (not required for raw syscalls here, but good hygiene).

Arguments can follow the **System V AMD64 ABI** (`rdi`, `rsi`, `rdx`, …) when interoperating with C; this chapter uses custom internal conventions for tiny examples.

exercises.title: Call prints
exercises.description: Put a procedure `say_hi` that performs one `write` of `Hi` (2 bytes, no newline). From `_start`, `call say_hi`, then exit 0.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .data
    msg: db 'H','i'
    mlen equ $ - msg
section .text
say_hi:
    ; rax=1 rdi=1 rsi=msg rdx=mlen syscall then ret
    ret
_start:
    ; call say_hi then exit
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
hints: `say_hi` must preserve registers you care about — here scratch `rax/rdi/rsi/rdx` freely
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .data
    msg: db 'H', 'i'
    mlen equ $ - msg
section .text
say_hi:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, msg
    mov rdx, mlen
    syscall
    ret
_start:
    call say_hi
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall

exercises.title: Tail of string
exercises.description: Write `tail` that takes pointer in `rdi` and length in `rsi`, issues `write` with those registers, then returns. `_start` passes address of bytes `OK` with length `2`.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .data
    buf: db 'O','K'
len equ $ - buf
section .text
tail:
    ; write(rdi, rsi) syscall layout: adjust to rax=1 rdi=1 stdout? exercise: stdout fd=1
    ret
_start:
    lea rdi, [rel buf]
    mov rsi, len
    call tail
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
hints: Inside `tail`, move `rdi`/`rsi` into the `rsi`/`rdx` slots for `write`, set `rdi=1`
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .data
    buf: db 'O', 'K'
len equ $ - buf
section .text
tail:
    mov rax, 1
    mov r8, rdi
    mov r9, rsi
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, r8
    mov rdx, r9
    syscall
    ret
_start:
    lea rdi, [rel buf]
    mov rsi, len
    call tail
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall

exercises.title: Nested calls
exercises.description: `outer` calls `inner` which prints `1` (one byte). Then `outer` returns to `_start` which exits 0.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .data
    one: db '1'
section .text
inner:
    ; write one byte '1'
    ret
outer:
    call inner
    ret
_start:
    call outer
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .data
    one: db '1'
section .text
inner:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    lea rsi, [rel one]
    mov rdx, 1
    syscall
    ret
outer:
    call inner
    ret
_start:
    call outer
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall

exercises.title: Counted stars
exercises.description: Procedure `emit_stars` takes the star count in **`rdi`** (here `4`). It fills a `.bss` buffer with that many `'*'` bytes and issues **one** `write` of length `rdi`. `_start` sets `rdi=4`, calls `emit_stars`, then exits 0. Expected stdout (trimmed) is `****`.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .bss
    buf: resb 32
section .text
emit_stars:
    ; save count in r12; loop i=0..count-1 mov byte [buf+i], '*'
    ; then write once: rdx = r12
    ret
_start:
    mov rdi, 4
    call emit_stars
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
hints: `syscall` clobbers `rcx` and `r11` — keep the count in a callee-saved reg like `r12`
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .bss
    buf: resb 32
section .text
emit_stars:
    mov r12, rdi
    xor rbx, rbx
fill:
    cmp rbx, r12
    jge done
    mov byte [rel buf+rbx], '*'
    inc rbx
    jmp fill
done:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    lea rsi, [rel buf]
    mov rdx, r12
    syscall
    ret
_start:
    mov rdi, 4
    call emit_stars
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
